reason: The two quotes state it is a Regional setting applying to all snapshots in the Region, must be enabled in each Region, is an account-level setting applying to all users, and cannot be enabled at the organization level.
The context lists exactly two modes; block all sharing makes already public snapshots private, block new sharing blocks only new sharing and already public snapshots remain public.
The quotes state charges are based on the size of the data backed up, not the source volume size, and subsequent incremental snapshots are charged only for changed and new data.
The tip recommends pausing writes, otherwise unmounting from within the instance, and says you can remount once the snapshot enters the pending state.

The quotes state you can copy snapshots between Regions, copy an unencrypted snapshot to an encrypted one, and copy snapshots shared with you privately or publicly; the completed-state condition is in the context.
The pricing page quote states copying is charged for data transferred across regions and standard snapshot storage charges apply in the destination region afterwards.
The table row under its header reads Disabled / Encrypted / Automatically encrypted, you can specify the KMS key, and without one the AWS managed key (aws/ebs) is used.
The quote states the copy is not automatically enabled for fast snapshot restore and you must explicitly enable it for the copy.
The quotes state same-account, same-Region, same-KMS-key copies are always incremental and that encrypting the copy with a different or new KMS key creates a full (non-incremental) copy.

The quotes support the full first copy to a new Region with extra storage cost, but the claim lists only some conditions for later incremental copies and drops the condition that the most recent copy has not been archived (and that it was copied there previously).
The quote states user-defined tags are not copied and can be added during or after the copy operation.
Under Snapshot destinations the quote states that if the source resource is in a Region, you must create snapshots in the same Region; the Local Zone and Outpost cases are separate bullets.
The quote states deleting a snapshot might not reduce storage costs because other snapshots might reference its data and referenced data is always preserved.
The quote states only data referenced exclusively by the snapshot is removed and deleting previous snapshots does not affect creating volumes from later snapshots.
The quote states a deleted snapshot matching a Recycle Bin retention rule is retained in the Recycle Bin instead of being immediately deleted.
The quote states that even though snapshots are incremental, the deletion process is designed so you need to retain only the most recent snapshot; the context ties this to restoring data.
The quote states the snapshot includes only data written at request time and not data cached by applications or the operating system.
The quote states snapshots are incremental backups saving only blocks changed after the most recent snapshot; the context confirms subsequent snapshots of the same volume are incremental.
Under Compliance mode the quote states after the cooling-off period you can't unlock, change the mode or decrease the duration, can only increase it, and must wait for the lock to expire to delete.
Under Cooling-off period the quote states it can range from 1 to 72 hours and omitting it locks in compliance mode immediately.
Under Lock duration, Number of days, the quote states the snapshot is automatically unlocked after the days pass and the duration ranges from 1 day to 36500 days (100 years).
Under Governance mode the quote states users with appropriate IAM permissions can unlock and modify mode and duration at any time, and the lock is immediate with no cooling-off period.
The quote states snapshots can be locked in compliance mode or governance mode, for a specific duration or until a specific date.
Under Pricing the quote states lock and unlock are at no additional cost and standard EBS snapshot storage costs apply to locked snapshots.
The quote states a locked snapshot can't be deleted by any user regardless of IAM permissions and can still be used like any other snapshot.
The quotes state only unencrypted snapshots can be shared publicly and public snapshots of encrypted volumes are not supported, but encrypted snapshots can be shared with specific accounts.
The quote states snapshots are constrained to their Region and to share with another Region you copy it there and share the copy.
The quote states you can't delete the root device snapshot used by a registered AMI, even if deprecated or disabled, and must deregister the AMI first.
The quote states snapshot data is automatically replicated across all AZs in the Region, enabling restore of volumes in any AZ in that Region.
The quotes state a volume from a snapshot is an exact copy at snapshot time and specifying a different AZ creates a duplicate volume in that zone.
The quote recommends stopping the instance before snapshotting a volume that serves as its root device.
The quote states snapshots are in S3 buckets you can't access directly, are managed with the EC2 console or API, and can't be accessed with the S3 console or API.
The quote states a snapshot gets the volume's encryption status; unencrypted volumes give unencrypted snapshots and encrypted volumes give snapshots encrypted with the same KMS key.
The quote states you must also share the customer managed key and can apply cross-account permissions to it at creation or later.

The quote and context state you modify snapshot permissions to share publicly with all accounts or privately with specified accounts, who can create their own volumes while the original is unaffected.
The quote states the standard rate for snapshots is $0.05 per GB-month, which applies once a snapshot is back in the standard tier; the qualifier marks it as the guide's example rate.
The quote states snapshots write a copy of the volume data to Amazon S3, where it is stored redundantly in multiple Availability Zones.
The quote states the volume does not need to be attached to a running instance in order to take a snapshot.
The quote states volume types are divided into two major categories: SSD-backed for transactional and HDD-backed for throughput intensive workloads.
The quote states for a 1-TiB st1 volume burst throughput is limited to 250 MiB/s and the bucket fills with credits at 40 MiB/s; the context says larger volumes scale linearly.
